source.title: Mean-field theory of graph neural networks in graph partitioning
source.authors: T. Kawamoto; Masashi Tsubaki; T. Obuchi

record.file_problem: None; full paper text is supplied.
record.tranche_reason: The paper trains a graph neural network by backpropagation and reports performance on a graph-partitioning task, extending the general question of how training affects network performance. Its overlap measure does not test the training classification-error outcomes named in the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper compares trained and untrained GNN performance on stochastic block models. The results concern graph-partitioning overlap and detectability, not training classification error on the benchmarks or the other measures named in V1–V6.
record.test_reason: The study uses residual shortcuts and batch normalization to train GNNs, then reports held-out graph-partitioning overlap and detectability. It does not measure the training-error, optimization-speed, initialization, minima, or stability effects specified by V1–V6. Its statement that deep GNNs cannot be learned correctly without ResNet and BN supplies neither a training-error comparison nor separate effects of the two techniques.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that untrained GNNs already perform well, backpropagation provides a quantitatively modest accuracy improvement, and the asymptotic detectability limit appears almost unchanged. They also emphasize readout sensitivity and non-negligible training cost.
record.recipe_differences: Backpropagation with an NMI error function and Adam on SBM graph-partitioning instances; the study evaluates overlap rather than the training classification error and image benchmarks in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Depth affects overlap; the authors report that deep GNN parameters (e.g., T > 25) cannot be learned correctly without ResNet and batch normalization. Readout choice also changes untrained GNN performance: using φ(X^T) gives overlap closer to the trained GNN than using X^T.

fits_no_version.finding: Deep trained GNNs improve held-out SBM partitioning overlap over the untrained comparator using X^T, while the detectability transition remains near epsilon = 0.33. Using tanh(X^T) substantially improves the untrained comparator and brings its performance close to the trained GNN.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For this SBM task, the finite-size partitioning advantage of a trained GNN depends on readout choice, while training appears to leave the asymptotic detectability threshold nearly unchanged.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors state that deep GNN parameters, for example beyond 25 layers, cannot be learned correctly without ResNet and batch normalization, but report no separate ablations or training-error values for that statement.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In this GNN training recipe, residual shortcuts and batch normalization jointly enable training at greater depth.

record.problems: The key comparisons are primarily shown in figures, and the text does not give exact overlap values or uncertainty for the trained-versus-untrained comparisons. The mean-field derivation relies on stated approximations.
record.rows_left_out: No additional separate training results were extracted: reported readout variants and figure curves do not provide distinct numeric results in the supplied text beyond the qualitative outcomes recorded in R1–R2.

untested.parts: Training classification error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including corrupted labels, and its dependence on model size or training recipe.
Spurious local minima and the effect of extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Depth-dependent training-error degradation in plain batch-normalized convolutional networks and prevention by identity shortcuts; special initialization and normalization-free residual training.
Initialization-dependent learning speed, signal and gradient propagation, and trainable depth.
Loss, curvature, recovery, and divergence relative to learning-rate stability thresholds.
Batch normalization's effect on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and comparison with Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: The qualitative trainability statement in Section 5.2 does not establish V3's specified degradation effect or V6's speed and learning-rate effects. No version-level verdict follows from it.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 training classification error, corrupted or random labels, model size, and early stopping or regularization.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious minima, and student width relative to teacher width.
Plain versus residual training classification error as a function of depth; the reported overlap measure does not test this version.
Activation-matched or orthogonal initialization effects on learning speed and trainable depth.
Learning-rate stability limits, curvature or sharpness, divergence, and training loss under squared-loss setups.
Batch normalization effects on accuracy speed or learning-rate tolerance in the specified image-classification settings, and Fixup comparisons.

rows.subject: GNN trained by backpropagation
rows.size_stated: Feature dimension D = 100; layers T varied (including T = 100); graph size N = 5,000 in the depth comparison.
rows.operation_detail: Train model parameters with Adam and the NMI error function; evaluate graph-partitioning overlap.
rows.baseline: Untrained GNN overlap; exact value not stated
rows.value: For sufficiently deep networks, overlap is clearly better than the untrained counterpart.
rows.note: Qualitative comparison stated in text; figure provides the curves, but no exact overlap values are given in the supplied text.
rows.check: The improvement in overlap is reported correctly, but it measures test-set graph partitioning rather than any version's optimization effect. The trained model uses both residual shortcuts and batch normalization; its untrained comparator uses k-means, so this is not an isolated comparison of parameter training.

rows.subject: GNN trained by backpropagation
rows.size_stated: Feature dimension D = 100; T = 100; graph sizes N = 312, 624, 1,250, 2,500, and 5,000.
rows.operation_detail: Train model parameters with Adam and the NMI error function; compare overlap transition across graph sizes.
rows.measure: Overlap with planted group assignments and location of deterioration as group-structure strength varies
rows.baseline: Untrained GNN detectability estimate; epsilon* approximately 0.33
rows.value: The region where overlap suddenly deteriorates still coincides with the untrained GNN mean-field estimate; exact overlap values not stated.
rows.note: The text states that the transition remains near the untrained estimate, but this overlap result does not measure any version's specified training-error outcome.
rows.check: The detectability result is correctly paraphrased but bears on none of V1–V6. The asymptotic conclusion is inferred from finite-size overlap curves, rather than directly measured at infinite graph size.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
